topic: Object File Analysis with GNU Binutils
explanation: Understanding the structure and contents of object files is crucial for systems programming and debugging.  GNU Binutils provide a suite of tools to inspect and manipulate these files, allowing programmers to analyze program behavior at a low level, identify performance bottlenecks, and debug system-level issues. This is vital for optimizing performance and understanding hardware-software interaction.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
nm my_object.o

readelf -h my_executable
readelf -S my_object.o  # Section Headers
readelf -s my_object.o  # Symbol Table
readelf -r my_object.o  # Relocations

objdump -d my_object.o   # Disassemble code sections (.text)
objdump -D my_executable # Disassemble all sections

objdump -t my_object.o   # Symbol table dump

size my_executable       # Segment sizes (text, data, bss)
size -A my_executable    # Detailed section sizes
keywords: GNU Binutils, Object file analysis, objdump, ELF format
